title: Automating sentinel-1 SLC product processing: Parallelization and optimization for efficient polarimetric parameter extraction
author: Fernando, Nketia, et al.

steps.title: Install and configure software
steps.instruction: Install Python 3.12.1, R 4.3.2 (with RStudio), SNAP 11.0.0, and PolSARpro v6.0 (version 6.0.4). Add each installation directory to the system PATH environment variable. Verify installations by running: `python --version` (expect 3.12.1), `R --version` (expect 4.3.2), `gpt --version` (SNAP CLI), and launch PolSARpro to confirm it starts.

steps.title: Download Sentinel‑1 SLC images
steps.instruction: Log in to the Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) Data Search platform with an Earth Data account. Use the auto‑generated Python script (provided in the repository readme) to bulk‑download the nine Sentinel‑1 SLC zip files acquired between 2021‑06‑10 and 2021‑07‑30 for the study area, executing the script from a local command‑prompt.

steps.title: Build base SNAP processing graph
steps.instruction: In SNAP, create a base graph that (1) reads a single S1 zip file, (2) extracts sub‑swaths with the TOPSAR‑Split tool, (3) applies precise orbit files (Apply‑Orbit‑File), (4) calibrates the data (Calibration), (5) debursts (TOPSAR‑Deburst), (6) applies Polarimetric‑Speckle‑Filter, (7) performs Terrain‑Correction, and (8) writes the result in PolSARpro format. Save this graph for reuse and later duplicate it for each IW swath (IW1, IW2, IW3).

steps.title: Prepare directories and modify SNAP graph
steps.instruction: Create an organized folder hierarchy for the workflow (e.g., raw, graphs, output). Using R’s `xml2` package, open the base SNAP graph XML file and edit it to select the desired Interferometric Wide (IW) swaths (IW1‑IW3). Save the modified base graph for subsequent duplication.

steps.title: Generate SNAP graphs for each image and swath
steps.instruction: For each of the nine S1 zip files and each of the three IW swaths, generate a dedicated SNAP graph XML file (total 27 graphs). Adjust the input and output file names in each graph so they reference the correct zip file and IW identifier.

steps.title: Run parallel SNAP graph processing
steps.instruction: In R, load the `parallelMap` library and register a parallel backend (e.g., `parallelStartSocket(cpus = 3)` to use three cores). Execute the 27 SNAP graphs concurrently, monitoring CPU and memory usage and adjusting the core count if needed to optimise throughput.

steps.title: Edit PolSARpro configuration file
steps.instruction: Open the PolSARpro `config.txt` file generated by SNAP and replace the parameter value `dual` with `pp2` so that PolSARpro recognises the C2 matrix files (.bin and .hdr). Save the edited file.

steps.title: Organize C2 folder and create reference TIFF
steps.instruction: Move all SNAP‑generated C2 matrix files (.bin and .hdr) into a new directory named `C2`. Using the header file `C11.hdr` as a spatial reference, create a GeoTIFF (e.g., `C11_ref.tif`) that preserves the geolocation metadata for the IW swath.

steps.title: Create valid‑pixel mask in PolSARpro
steps.instruction: Run PolSARpro’s `create_mask_valid_pixels` tool on the C2 files to generate a mask that flags only valid pixels for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Compute C2 covariance matrix elements
steps.instruction: Execute PolSARpro’s `process_elements` tool to calculate the four C2 elements: C11 = |SVV|², C22 = |SVH|², C12 = SVV·SVH* (cross‑correlation), and C21 = SVH·SVV* (complex conjugate of C12).

steps.title: Calculate total span and Stokes parameters
steps.instruction: Run `process_span` to obtain Span = C11 + C22. Then run `stokes_parameters` to compute: g0 = |SVV|² + |SVH|², g1 = |SVV|² – |SVH|², g2 = 2·Re(SVV·SVH*), g3 = 2·Im(SVV·SVH*).

steps.title: Derive Stokes angles, DoLP, LPR, eigenvalues
steps.instruction: From the Stokes values, calculate orientation angle ψ = ½·atan(g2/g1) and ellipticity angle χ = ½·atan(g3/g0). Extract eigenvalues λ1 and λ2 of the C2 matrix. Compute Degree of Linear Polarization DoLP = (g1² + g2²)/g0 and Linear Polarization Ratio LPR = |SVV|² / |SVH|².

steps.title: Perform H‑α decomposition
steps.instruction: Use PolSARpro’s `h_a_alpha_decompositionSPPC2` tool to obtain Entropy H = –∑ pᵢ log₂ pᵢ (where pᵢ are eigen‑value‑derived probabilities), Alpha angle α = ∑ pᵢ αᵢ, and the Shannon Entropy of the scattering process.

steps.title: Generate ENVI .hdr files for PolSARpro outputs
steps.instruction: For each PolSARpro‑generated .bin file (e.g., C11, C12_imag, C12_real, C22), create a matching ENVI‑compatible .hdr file by copying the spatial metadata (rows, columns, map info) from the reference `C11.hdr` and adapting the filename accordingly.

steps.title: Rasterize outputs to GeoTIFF
steps.instruction: Convert each .bin/.hdr pair into a raster GeoTIFF using a GIS tool (e.g., GDAL `gdal_translate`), ensuring that the geospatial coordinates from the .hdr files are retained so the final rasters align correctly with geographic reference data.
